etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English taillour, from Anglo-Norman taillour, from Old French tailleor, from taillier, from Late Latin tāliō, from Latin tālea (“a cutting”). Doublet of tailleur.

definitions.definition: A person who makes, repairs, or alters clothes professionally, especially suits and men's clothing.

quote.citation: 1880, New South Wales. Parliament. Legislative Council, Journal (volume 30, part 3, page 460)
quote.text: The tailor — is that a sea fish — a line fish? It is a sea fish, but not a line fish. They will bite at a line, but they are not a fish you can depend on with the line.

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To make, repair, or alter clothes.
(transitive) To make or adapt (something) for a specific need.
(transitive) To restrict (something) in order to meet a particular need.
